findings: Coverage gate is vacuous in this summary: coverage.measured is all-null and the packages/desktop override reports passed_count 0/69 with pass=true, while both atomic reports record coverage.pass=false (vite-plus functions 88.76 < 90; rust branches 0 < 85) - the rollup ingested no per-file coverage, so the configured 90/85/90 thresholds were not actually enforced and the pass conclusion overstates the coverage state.

Rust branch coverage reads 0 because cargo llvm-cov ran without branch instrumentation, so the rust atomic coverage gate fails on branches (0 < 85) for a tooling reason rather than a real gap; run llvm-cov with --branch or map rust branches to null (as go-cover does) so the dimension is not falsely evaluated.

Rust mutation was not measured: the summary mutation block covers only vite-plus (override file_count 69, passed_count 69) and the rust atomic report has mutation: null, although config.json declares a rust mutation score of 70 - the rust half of the change (store/workflow/orchestration/commands crates) has no mutation evidence.

Rust test count is under-reported: the report counts 81 tests, but results.txt from the same cargo test --workspace run records 30 test binaries totaling 1424 passing tests (the 81 matches only the first binary, core/workflow state_test), so summary total 1053 understates the real executed suite size (972 + 1424 = 2396).

All reported tests pass (vite-plus 972/972, rust 81/81 as counted; 0 failed, 0 skipped across both raw outputs) and vite-plus mutation passes at 84.22% vs the 80% threshold (870 killed / 1075 total; 149 survived + 14 noCoverage).
